blocks.text: Visitors by a river and waterfall in the forest near Arenal, Costa Rica
Arenal, Costa Rica: a waterfall, rushing river and visitors on the rocky bank

Today you'll take a guided hike in the Río Celeste area. From Arenal Volcano, it's about a 1.5-hour drive through the countryside to the park.

Río Celeste lies near the Tenorio and Miravalles volcanoes and is known for its bright blue water. On arrival, you'll set out through the dense tropical rainforest of Tenorio Volcano National Park. Your nature guide can adjust the pace to suit the group and will explain the plants and forest ecosystems along the way.

One of the main stops is Los Teñideros, where two streams meet. The water's striking turquoise-blue colour is especially noticeable here. According to a local Maleku legend, after God painted the sky, he dipped his brush in the river and turned it blue. The scientific explanation attributes the effect to suspended particles containing aluminium, silicon and oxygen that affect the way light refracts in the water.

Along the way you'll see the rainforest and the Río Celeste waterfall.

Meals: Breakfast.
